title: An Urban Refuge for Threatened Cacti: Diversity and Conservation of the Cactaceae Collection at FES-Cuautitlan Botanical Garden, UNAM
content: The Cactaceae represent one of the most diverse and threatened plant families worldwide, with Mexico constituting their principal center of diversity and endemism. Botanical gardens play a fundamental role in the ex situ conservation of this unique flora by maintaining living collections that support research, education, and species preservation. This study presents the first comprehensive taxonomic inventory and conservation assessment of the cactus collection maintained at the Botanical Garden of the Facultad de Estudios Superiores Cuautitlan, Universidad Nacional Autonoma de Mexico (UNAM). Between January 2024 and June 2025, all living specimens were inventoried and taxonomically verified, and their conservation status was evaluated according to the IUCN Red List, NOM-059-SEMARNAT-2010, and the CITES Appendices. The collection comprises 342 taxa belonging to 62 genera, including 259 native species, of which 215 are endemic to Mexico, and 83 exotic taxa. According to the IUCN Red List, most taxa were classified as Least Concern (180), although the collection also includes 106 threatened taxa, comprising 45 Vulnerable, 41 Endangered, and 20 Critically Endangered species. Additionally, 4 taxa are Near Threatened, 6 are Data Deficient, and 46 have not yet been evaluated. Under NOM-059-SEMARNAT, 65 taxa are listed as Endangered (P) and 47 are under Special Protection (Pr), highlighting the high conservation value of the collection at both national and international levels. These findings demonstrate that the FESC Botanical Garden houses an exceptional repository of Mexican cactus diversity and represents an important resource for ex situ conservation, scientific research, environmental education, and the long-term preservation of threatened plant genetic resources.
